question: Should `socket.drain` be a best-effort hint with mandatory state resynchronization, or a reliably replayable teardown signal with its own delivery guarantees?
rationale: The current Gateway transport intentionally bounds slow clients by dropping frames or closing connections; selecting a recovery contract changes public protocol behavior and cannot be resolved safely as a mechanical code fix.

options.title: Best-effort plus resync
options.body: Preserve bounded shedding and require clients to rebuild authoritative session state through `sessions.list` or a state-version check after gaps and reconnects.

options.title: Durable drain replay
options.body: Add a bounded sequence, replay, or acknowledgment mechanism so teardown events survive slow buffers and reconnects.

options.title: Accept close-on-overflow
options.body: Keep the proposed behavior, explicitly document that slow clients may disconnect and must retain an independent polling or reconciliation fallback.

recommendation.title: Best-effort plus resync
recommendation.body: Preserve bounded shedding and require clients to rebuild authoritative session state through `sessions.list` or a state-version check after gaps and reconnects.
